mainTopic: Whether a pouring stream (נצוק) is a חיבור, and practical rules for pouring and drinking wine with gentiles
overview: The גמרא tries to answer a question it already raised: does a pouring stream (נצוק) connect two vessels into one unit (חיבור)? A proof from the funnel case in the משנה is blocked by רבי חייא, who places that case where the wine touched the funnel directly. A proof from pouring vessel to vessel is defended at first, then dropped, because the סיפא of the same משנה points the other way. A ברייתא about pouring from a barrel into a pit is explained by רב ששת as a case of כח גוי, a rule the רבנן limited to wine that leaves the barrel. רבא's ruling forbidding a whole barrel after a gentile touched a siphon tube is also set aside as a special case. So the question of נצוק is not settled on this amud. Along the way come practical rulings: break up the stream when pouring for gentiles, and keep a gentile from helping you pour. The amud ends with the rule that a Jew and a gentile may drink together from קנישקנין, as long as the Jew stops first.

steps.title: Proof from the leftover wine in the funnel
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says wine left in the funnel is forbidden. The only thing that could forbid it is the stream running down into the gentile's vessel, so נצוק must be חיבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there is leftover wine in the funnel, it is forbidden. How did that leftover wine become forbidden? Wasn't it through the stream? Learn from this: a stream is a connection.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a funnel used to pour wine into a gentile's vessel. It tries to use that case to prove that a stream counts as a connection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wine stuck in the funnel never touched the gentile's vessel directly. The only link between them is the stream pouring down. If the leftover wine is forbidden, the stream must be what connects it to the gentile's wine.

keyTerms.meaning: Leftover wine that stays stuck in the funnel
A connection that makes two things count as one unit
Learn from this (a proof is being drawn)

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ בּוֹ עַכֶּבֶת יַיִן — אָסוּר.
phrases.english: If there is a remnant of wine in it, it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: "In it" means in the funnel the משנה talks about, the one used to pour wine into a gentile's vessel.

phrases.aramaic: הָא עַכֶּבֶת יַיִן בְּמַאי קָא מִתַּסְרָא?
phrases.english: This remnant of wine, through what does it become forbidden?
Is it not through the stream?
Learn from it: a stream is a connection.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier question of whether נצוק is חיבור by bringing a proof from the משנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's ruling that leftover wine in the funnel is forbidden

steps.title: רבי חייא: the gentile's wine rose up to the funnel
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא teaches that the משנה is talking about a case where the wine in the gentile's jug rose up and touched the funnel. If so, there was direct contact, and the stream is not needed to explain the ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא taught: this is a case where his jug pressed up against it.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא from רבי חייא narrows the case of the משנה. This undercuts the proof from step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the gentile's wine actually rose up and touched the funnel, the funnel's wine became forbidden through direct contact. Then the משנה tells us nothing about whether a stream connects.

keyTerms.meaning: His jug reached it, meaning the wine in the jug rose up to the funnel

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya taught:
Where his jug reached it,
phrases.notes: The wine in the gentile's jug filled up until it touched the funnel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Undermines the proof by placing the משנה in a case of direct contact.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the funnel case
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה may be speaking about direct contact, not about a stream.

steps.title: Inference from רבי חייא that a stream does not connect
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from רבי חייא's teaching: if the jug did not reach the funnel, the wine is permitted. That would prove the opposite, that נצוק is not חיבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if his jug did not reach it, what is the law? Isn't it permitted? Then resolve it: a stream is not a connection!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns רבי חייא's teaching into a proof for the other side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא specified a case of direct contact. That suggests that without contact, with only a stream, the wine is permitted. If so, the stream does not connect.

phrases.english: But if his jug did not reach it, what is the law?
Not forbidden; so resolve that a stream is not a connection!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an opposite conclusion from רבי חייא's limitation.
steps.raayaSupportSource: An inference from רבי חייא's teaching

steps.title: No proof either way: the question stays open
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the inference. רבי חייא only teaches the clear case, contact, which is surely forbidden. The case of a stream is still an open question.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. When his jug reached it, you can resolve that it is forbidden. A stream, though, remains a question.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks the inference from step 3. It leaves the question of נצוק unanswered for now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא chose the case of contact because that one is certain. He did not mean that a stream is permitted. He simply left that case undecided.

phrases.english: No; where his jug reached it,
you can resolve that it is forbidden,
but a stream remains a question.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, פְּחָסַתּוּ צְלוֹחִיתוֹ — תִּפְשׁוֹט לָךְ דְּאָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The inference that נצוק is not חיבור
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי חייא only stated the certain case. He did not rule on the stream.
steps.whatToRemember: The funnel case proves nothing either way. רבי חייא puts it in a case of direct contact, so the question of נצוק is still open.

steps.title: Proof from pouring from one vessel to another
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that when pouring from one vessel to another, the wine in the upper vessel is permitted. This implies that the wine in mid-air is forbidden, so נצוק is חיבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: one who pours from vessel to vessel, the wine in the vessel he pours from is permitted. This implies that what is in between is forbidden. Learn from this: a stream is a connection.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new proof, this time from the second case in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only permits the wine still inside the upper vessel. The wine in the falling stream is left out, which implies it is forbidden. It can only be forbidden because the stream connects it to the gentile's vessel below.

phrases.english: Come and hear: one who pours from vessel to vessel,
that which he pours from is permitted,
implying that what is in between is forbidden.
phrases.notes: "In between" is the wine in the falling stream, between the two vessels.

phrases.english: Learn from it: a stream is a connection.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof failed, a new proof is brought.
steps.raayaSupportSource: An inference from the משנה's case of pouring from vessel to vessel

steps.title: Then the upper vessel's wine should be forbidden too
steps.stepSummary: If the stream connects, it should connect the wine in the upper vessel as well. Yet the משנה permits that wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a stream is a connection, even the wine inside the vessel should also be forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof in step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The stream runs unbroken from the upper vessel down to the lower one. If it links the falling wine to the gentile's vessel, it should link the upper vessel's wine too. The משנה permits that wine, so the proof seems to work against itself.

phrases.english: If a stream is a connection,
even what is inside the vessel should also be forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נִצּוֹק חִיבּוּר, אֲפִילּוּ דְּגַוֵּיהּ דְּמָנָא נָמֵי לִיתְּסַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof of step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof that נצוק is חיבור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the stream connects, it should forbid the upper vessel's wine, which the משנה permits.

steps.title: He pours in broken spurts
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is talking about someone who breaks up the flow. The stream is cut off from the upper vessel, so that wine stays permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult: he is pouring in interrupted spurts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by describing how the pouring is done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The upper vessel's wine is permitted because the stream gets broken. That is not because a stream fails to connect. The wine already falling is still forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: He interrupts the flow, pouring in breaks

phrases.english: This is not difficult,
for he interrupts the flow.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא, דְּקָא מְקַטֵּיף קַטּוֹפֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The upper vessel's wine being permitted shows a stream does not connect.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is permitted only because the flow is broken.

steps.title: The proof seems to stand: a stream is a connection
steps.stepSummary: Either way, the proof stands: נצוק is חיבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, a stream is a connection!
steps.whatsHappening: After answering the challenge, the גמרא restates the proof from step 5. The next step will reject it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Interrupted pouring explains why the upper wine is permitted. The falling wine is still forbidden, and that shows a stream connects.

phrases.english: In any case, a stream is a connection!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the proof after the challenge has been answered.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Within this line of reasoning, נצוק is חיבור and the upper wine is permitted only because the pouring is broken up. Step 9 then cancels the proof.
steps.whatToRemember: For now the vessel-to-vessel proof seems to hold: a pouring stream connects, and the upper vessel's wine is permitted only because the flow is broken. The next step overturns this proof.

steps.title: The end of the same משנה points the other way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the last clause of the same משנה suggests the opposite inference. So no proof can be drawn from that משנה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your reasoning, read the last clause: only the wine he poured into is forbidden. That suggests the wine in between is permitted! So nothing can be learned from this משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from step 8. If we read the end of the משנה the same way, it seems to say the stream in mid-air is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause made it sound like the stream is forbidden. The last clause names only the lower vessel as forbidden, which makes it sound like the stream is permitted. When two clauses of one משנה point in opposite directions, neither one proves anything.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning: turning the other side's logic against them
The last clause of a משנה or ברייתא
In between: here, the wine in mid-air between the two vessels
There is nothing to learn from it

steps.confusionAlert: Step 8 seemed to settle that נצוק is חיבור. This step cancels that proof. The question is open again.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning, say the latter clause:
It is the one into which he poured that is forbidden,
which implies that what is in between is permitted!
Rather, nothing can be learned from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Cancels the proof that step 8 had confirmed
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the משנה about pouring from vessel to vessel
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two clauses of the משנה give opposite inferences, so neither one decides the question

steps.title: A new proof from pouring a barrel into a pit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: when someone pours from a barrel into a pit, the stream leaving the barrel is forbidden. This seems to show that נצוק is חיבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if someone pours from a barrel into a pit, the stream coming down from the barrel's rim is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new source to prove that a stream connects. The stream is forbidden even before it reaches the pit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why would the stream in mid-air be forbidden? It seems to be because it is connected to the forbidden wine in the pit below. That would mean נצוק is חיבור.

keyTerms.meaning: A pit or cistern for wine

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who pours from a barrel into a pit,
phrases.notes: The case assumes the wine already in the pit is forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: קִילּוּחַ הַיּוֹרֵד מִשְּׂפַת חָבִית לְמַטָּה — אָסוּר!
phrases.english: the stream that goes down from the rim of the barrel downward is forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the funnel proof and the vessel-to-vessel proof both failed, the גמרא brings a third source
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about pouring from a barrel into a pit

steps.title: רב ששת: the pourer is a gentile
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that the ברייתא is about a gentile doing the pouring. The stream is forbidden because it comes from the gentile's force, not because of any connection.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת explained it as a case where a gentile is pouring, so the wine comes out through his force.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת turns aside the proof. He gives a different reason the stream is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine moved by a gentile's force is forbidden, even if he never touches it. So the stream is forbidden for that reason. The ברייתא says nothing about whether a stream connects.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained it: read the source in a specific way
His force: wine moved by the gentile's action

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet explained it:
as a case of a gentile who pours, since it comes from his force.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 10 by explaining the case differently
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the barrel-and-pit ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The stream may be forbidden because of כח גוי, not because of חיבור

steps.title: Then the wine inside the barrel should be forbidden too
steps.stepSummary: If a gentile is pouring, his force moves the whole barrel. So the wine still inside the barrel should also be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a gentile is pouring, even the wine inside the barrel should be forbidden too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב ששת's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gentile's force is acting on all the wine in the barrel, not just the stream. So why does the ברייתא forbid only the stream coming out?

phrases.english: If a gentile is the one pouring,
even the inside of the barrel should also become forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי גּוֹי הַמְעָרֶה, אֲפִילּוּ גַּוָּא דְּחָבִיתָא נָמֵי מִתְּסַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב ששת's explanation
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's explanation that the pourer is a gentile
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The gentile's force moves all the wine, so the ברייתא should forbid the wine in the barrel too, not just the stream

steps.title: The rabbinic decree covers only wine that left the barrel
steps.stepSummary: Wine becomes forbidden through כח גוי only by rabbinic law. The רבנן made the decree only for wine that came out, not for wine that stayed inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: A gentile's force forbids wine only by rabbinic law. The רבנן decreed on wine that went out, but they did not decree on wine that stayed inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב ששת. The decree of כח גוי was limited from the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since כח גוי is a rabbinic rule, the רבנן decided how far it reaches. They limited it to wine that actually left the barrel. That explains why the ברייתא forbids only the stream.

keyTerms.meaning: A gentile's force: wine moved by a gentile's action

steps.whatToRemember: Wine is forbidden through כח גוי only by rabbinic law, and only the wine that comes out. So the barrel ברייתא no longer proves that נצוק is חיבור.

phrases.english: A gentile's force forbids only by rabbinic law;

phrases.aramaic: הַהוּא דִּנְפַק לְבָרַאי — גְּזַרוּ בֵּיהּ רַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: on the wine that went outside, the Rabbis decreed;

phrases.aramaic: הַהוּא דִּלְגַוַּאי — לָא גְּזַרוּ בֵּיהּ רַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: on the wine that is inside, the Rabbis did not decree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the reach of a rabbinic decree
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The gentile's force should forbid all the wine he moves, even inside the barrel
steps.terutzMaskana: The rabbinic decree applies only to wine that left the barrel

steps.title: רב חסדא: break up the stream when selling to gentiles
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא tells wine sellers to pour in short bursts, or toss the wine out all at once, when measuring wine for gentiles.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא told the wine sellers: when you measure wine for gentiles, pour in broken spurts, or toss it out all at once.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings practical instructions. רב חסדא tells sellers to avoid a steady stream.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A steady stream could link the seller's wine to the gentile's vessel. That fits the worry that נצוק is חיבור. Breaking the flow, as in step 7, cuts that link.

keyTerms.meaning: Toss it out in one motion

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב חִסְדָּא לְהָנְהוּ סָבֹיָתָא:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said to those wine sellers:
When you measure wine for gentiles,
pour in broken spurts,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: or alternatively, toss it out in one go.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב חִסְדָּא לְהָנְהוּ סָבֹיָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from discussing sources to practical guidance
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When pouring wine for gentiles, do not pour in a steady stream

steps.title: רבא: do not let a gentile help you pour
steps.stepSummary: רבא warns pourers not to let a gentile help. You might rest the vessel on him, and then the wine would come out through his force and be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא told the pourers: when you pour wine, do not let a gentile come close to help you. You might become distracted and rest the vessel on him. Then the wine comes out through his force and is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a practical warning based on the rule of כח גוי from step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine that comes out through a gentile's force is forbidden by rabbinic decree. If the pourer leans the vessel on the gentile, the gentile's force becomes part of the pouring. So it is safest to keep him away entirely.

keyTerms.meaning: You rest or throw it on

steps.whatToRemember: In practice: break up the stream when pouring for gentiles, and keep a gentile's force out of the pouring.

phrases.english: Rava said to those wine pourers:
When you pour wine,
do not let a gentile come close to help you,
lest you get distracted and rest it on him,
phrases.notes: "It" is the vessel of wine you are pouring from.

phrases.english: and it comes out through his force and is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second practical instruction, this one based on the rule of כח גוי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not let a gentile help with pouring wine, in case the wine comes out through his force

steps.title: A gentile touches the siphon tube and רבא forbids all the wine
steps.stepSummary: A man was drawing wine out of a barrel with a large tube and a small tube. A gentile rested his hand on the large tube, and רבא forbade all of the wine, including what was still in the barrel.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man was siphoning wine with a big tube and a small tube. A gentile came and put his hand on the big tube. רבא forbade all the wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case. רבא gave a surprisingly strict ruling: even the wine still sitting in the barrel is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, the סוגיא said that only wine that actually came out through the gentile's force is forbidden. Here רבא forbids even the wine left in the barrel. That ruling invites the question in the next step: why should the wine inside be forbidden?

keyTerms.meaning: A large tube used to siphon wine out of a barrel
A small tube, the companion of the large siphon tube

phrases.english: A certain man who drew up wine
with a large tube and a small tube;
a gentile came and rested his hand on the large tube;
Rava forbade all of the wine.
phrases.notes: "All" includes the wine still inside the barrel, not only what already came out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a practical case about wine leaving a vessel, the same subject as the rulings of רב חסדא and רבא in steps 14-15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a gentile rests his hand on a siphon tube, רבא forbids all of the wine, including the wine left in the barrel.

steps.title: Does this ruling prove that a pouring stream connects the wine?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא, or רב אדא בר מתנה, or רבינא asks רבא how the wine in the barrel became forbidden. If the answer is through the stream, then we should learn that נצוק is חיבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: One of the אמוראים asked רבא: How did the barrel become forbidden? Through the stream? If so, should we learn that a stream counts as a connection?
steps.whatsHappening: Someone tries to learn a big general rule from רבא's ruling: that a stream of liquid joins the wine above it to the wine below it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning goes like this. The gentile's touch forbade the wine in the tube. The only way that could spread to the wine still in the barrel is if the flowing stream links them. That would mean נצוק is חיבור.

keyTerms.meaning: A pouring stream counts as a connection between the two vessels

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Rava,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָה לְרָבָא,
phrases.english: and some say it was Rav Adda bar Mattana to Rava,
and some say it was Ravina to Rava:
Through what did the barrel become forbidden? Through the stream.
Should you conclude from this that a stream is a connection?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to draw a general principle from רבא's ruling in step 16.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's ruling forbidding all of the wine in the barrel

steps.title: A siphon is different because all the wine is pulled toward the tubes
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. In a siphon, all the wine in the barrel is being drawn toward the tubes, so the gentile's touch affects all of it. This case teaches nothing about an ordinary stream.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because all the wine is being pulled into the large tube and the small tube.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back the proof from step 17. His ruling was based on how a siphon works, not on the rule of נצוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a siphon, the whole barrel is one moving body of wine flowing into the tubes. So touching the tube is like touching all the wine in the barrel. With ordinary pouring, the wine in the upper vessel is not being pulled the same way, so no general rule of חיבור can be learned here.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there: the case has a special feature

steps.whatToRemember: רבא forbade the whole barrel because a siphon pulls all the wine toward the tubes. We cannot learn from his ruling that נצוק is חיבור.

phrases.english: It is different there,

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי חַמְרָא אַגִּישְׁתָּא וּבַת גִּישְׁתָּא גְּרִיר.
phrases.english: because all the wine is drawn toward the large tube and the small tube.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference proposed in step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning a general rule of נצוק חיבור from the siphon case
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The siphon case has a special feature: the whole barrel is pulled toward the tubes, so it is like the gentile touched all the wine.

steps.title: Drinking together from a multi-tube vessel is allowed if the Jew stops first
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא בריה דרב נחמן rules that a Jew and a gentile may drink at the same time from קנישקנין. This is only when the Jew stops drinking first. If the gentile stops first, it is not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא son of רב נחמן said: A vessel with several drinking tubes is permitted. But that is only when the Jew stops first. If the gentile stops first, it is not permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling: a Jew and a gentile can share a vessel that has several drinking tubes, with one condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Jew stops first, he has finished drinking before any wine can slide back from the gentile's tube. If the gentile stops first, wine from his mouth and tube can flow back into the shared vessel while the Jew is still drinking. That would make the wine forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A vessel with several tubes so several people can drink at once
And this applies only when: introduces a limit on the rule

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as a general permission to drink with a gentile from one vessel. It works only when the Jew is the one who stops first.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Mar Zutra, son of Rav Naḥman, said:
A vessel with several drinking tubes is permitted,
phrases.notes: He means a Jew and a gentile drinking from it at the same time.

phrases.english: and this applies only where the Jew stopped first,
but if the gentile stopped first, not.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Drinking together from קנישקנין is permitted only if the Jew stops drinking before the gentile.

steps.title: רבה בר רב הונא allows multi-tube drinking at the house of the ריש גלותא
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא visited the house of the ריש גלותא and permitted them to drink with קנישקנין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא came to the house of the ריש גלותא and allowed them to drink from a multi-tube vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story showing that a great sage actually allowed people to use קנישקנין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story backs up מר זוטרא's ruling with real practice. The permission was given in a public, important setting, the house of the ריש גלותא. That shows the ruling was really followed in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: The house of the Exilarch, leader of the Jews in Bavel

steps.whatToRemember: A multi-tube vessel may be shared with a gentile, as long as the Jew stops first. רבה בר רב הונא allowed it in practice.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that מר זוטרא's ruling was not only theory. It was used in practice.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna happened to come to the house of the Exilarch;
he permitted them to drink with a multi-tube vessel.
phrases.notes: "Them" means the people there, drinking together with gentiles.
